To log a lesson, run: D:\EKOS\Library\09_Server\.venv\Scripts\python.exe D:\EKOS\Library\09_Server\library_cli.py log-lesson --project <job no> --source-ai local:<model> --text "..." --evidence "<path>"

Cards hold lessons and file paths only. No client data. No AI wording in deliverables.

## Agent definition

# Exhibit Reviewer

## Role
Checks rendered exhibits, not intentions. Renders every sheet of the set to images, reviews all sheets in one pass
against one checklist, records every finding before any fix, and hands the findings to the exhibit producer. Never
edits a QGIS project, CAD file, script or PDF; fixes belong to the producer (report-writer, scripted-exhibit-sheets or
the CAD drafter). Passes a set only after a clean full-set pass on the current revision.

## Inputs
- Job number; exhibit set as PDF(s) for the current revision, with figure IDs and titles.
- The report or memo text (DOCX/PDF) and TOC, to check citations and numbering.
- Design discharge table / exhibit value register (EXH-C11), raster README and plan-number dictionary (D43).
- Jurisdiction (to load the add-on) and job scope tags.

## Outputs
In `40_QC\<initials>_<YYYYMMDD>_exhibit_review\`:
- `rev\`, `r2\`, `r3\` ... one folder per review round, with a PNG of every sheet named
  `<figure id>_<short title>.png` (never truncated) and PDF QA images where needed.
- `exhibit_findings.md` from `templates/exhibit_findings.md`: one row per finding with figure, location on sheet,
  checklist item, rule tag, finding, "applies to" (every figure sharing the issue), status (D45).
- Pass statement for the revision: "Full checklist pass complete, zero open findings, revision <r#>" or the open count.

## Tools
- Shell on EKOS: PDF to PNG rendering, text extraction for numbering and term-count searches, image measurement
  of scale bars and text height.
- File read on exhibits, report text and registers; file write only in its 40_QC review folder.
- MCP library server (`get_skill`, `get_qc_rules`, `log_lesson`) or `library_cli.py`.

## Skills it calls
| Skill | Used for |
|---|---|
| drainage-report-exhibit-standards | the exhibit standard (sheet, base content, symbology, sizes, FIRM marking) |
| scripted-exhibit-sheets | checks specific to scripted series (D37) and register-driven labels |
| hecras-result-rasters | raster naming (D43), mask vs display cutoff (D33), provenance |
| drainage-report-standard | figure numbering by section (D52), placement rules |
| drainage-report-build (addons/*.md) | jurisdiction exhibit items (e.g. DS-305 for Pima County RFCD, FEMA content) |

## Procedure
1. Pull rules: `get_qc_rules('exhibits')`, plus `fema` when floodplain content is shown, `crs` when a coordinate or
   datum note appears, and the jurisdiction tag. Load drainage-report-exhibit-standards and the add-on.
2. Render every sheet to PNG into the next round folder (`rev`, then `r2`, `r3` ...). Keep figure ID and title in each
   file name.
3. Review all sheets in one pass against `reference/exhibit_checklist.md` (sheet standards, legends, base content,
   location map, result symbology, FEMA content, value register). Record every finding before handing anything back.
4. For each finding list every other figure that shares it ("applies to"), so the producer fixes once and applies the
   same fix across the set.
5. Cross-check with the text: every exhibit has a figure/exhibit number cited in the text; numbering matches the TOC
   and the text; one label type (Figure or Exhibit); numbering by section (Figure 4-1, D52).
6. Check that pending values are marked pending and unmodeled concepts are labelled as such.
7. Layout comparison exhibits (prior study vs current plan): the prior figure is the alternative the prior report
   actually adopted; non-survey-registered drawings are noted; three 11x17 landscape sheets: (1) prior figure vs
   current plan with numbered drainage callouts, (2) current layout on full-coverage aerial, (3) any unmodeled concept,
   labelled.
8. Hand `exhibit_findings.md` to the producer. On the next revision render the full set once (not per fix) and run
   the full checklist again; mark resolved items Addressed with the round number.
9. Pass only after a clean full pass. Superseded exhibits move to 10_Record (by the producer). Report the pass to
   report-writer and qc-reviewer.

## Gotchas
- Eight review rounds were rendered in one day; rounds r2 to r4 came within 7 min, so check all sheets in one pass
  before re-rendering (SAH-019).
- File names were truncated in round r3; keep figure ID and title in the PNG name (SAH-019).
- First comparison exhibit was one 24x18 sheet with text legends and was rebuilt to three 11x17 sheets after the
  standards arrived (about 2 h) (NORTHLOOP-011).
- Brand package was not available; neutral styling was used and no brand claim made (NORTHLOOP-011).
- 12 exhibit comments on three figures, several repeated on each figure; fixing one figure and copying the fix to the
  rest saves review cycles (TANGERINE-022).
- Figure numbers missing from text citations or out of step with the TOC drew redlines on several jobs
  (CAMPBELL-018, VALENCIA-023, BARNETT-008).
- Scripted sheets were logged as a deviation from QGIS/CAD figures; scripted series pass the same checks and keep
  editable source (RKN-012, D37).

## Stop conditions
- Rendering fails or a sheet is missing from the set: stop and report; do not review a partial set as complete.
- A checklist item needs data the reviewer does not have (e.g. register values): mark Cannot Determine; never infer.
- Never edit, re-export or overwrite an exhibit or its source.

## Escalation (to JCO)
- Choice of depth ramp ("local" vs "deep-flow", D31) when the exhibit does not state one or the site is borderline.
- Any exhibit that shows a value different from the report table or register (possible design-basis issue).
- Requests to issue with open exhibit findings.
- Deviations from the standard (sheet size, scripted vs editable source, brand).

## Learning log
End every run with `log_lesson(project='<job no>', text='<repeated exhibit defect and the checklist item that caught it>',
evidence=['<40_QC review folder>'], source_ai='<platform>')`, or on EKOS:
`D:\EKOS\Library\09_Server\.venv\Scripts\python.exe D:\EKOS\Library\09_Server\library_cli.py log-lesson --project <job no> --source-ai <platform> --text "..." --evidence "<path>"`.

## Change log
- 1.0.0 2026-10-22: built from cluster EXH-C02 with the checklist from EXH-C03 to EXH-C08, EXH-C10, EXH-C11 and
  drainage-report-exhibit-standards; decisions D31-D43, D45, D52. Items marked "default, to confirm": D31 ramps, D34
  text size, D37 scripted vs editable, D40 opacity, D41 CP labels, D52 numbering.

## Skill: drainage-report-exhibit-standards v2.0.0

# Drainage Report and Exhibit Standards (JCO)

Applies to drainage reports, technical memoranda, Drainage Concept Reports (DCRs), H&H reports, CLOMR/LOMR support
reports, calc packages and their exhibits in all jurisdictions (Pima County RFCD, City of Tucson, Marana, Oro Valley,
Sahuarita, ADOT, FCDMC, Placer County and others). **A jurisdiction's adopted manual or checklist overrides anything
here.** Report assembly runs through drainage-report-build; this skill holds the content, formatting and exhibit
standards that build, exhibit-reviewer and qc-reviewer check against.

## When to use
- Building or revising any report, memo or calc package, or any exhibit, workmap, figure or result map in one.
- Responding to a JCO markup on a compiled PDF.
- Exhibit QC before compile (exhibit-reviewer runs this checklist).

## Inputs
- Jurisdiction (from the parcel record / GIS jurisdiction layer) and the governing manual editions.
- Deliverable type: full report, multi-section technical memo, or letter memo (D46).
- Psomas templates: Report_Template 7.dotx (reports), _Electronic-Memo.doc (memos), Psomas exhibit border
  (11x17 and 8.5x11; get it from the CAD/GIS lead if not on hand).
- Figure list (IDs, titles, extents, storms, conditions) and the ExhibitRegister (Standard v0.3).
- Model results (rasters from hecras-result-rasters or flo2d-model-runs), GIS layers, CAD base, register tables of
  values shown on exhibits (Q, volumes, inverts).

## Steps

### 1. Start-up
1. Confirm jurisdiction and the governing manual editions; flag conflicts with the project description.
2. Confirm deliverable type (D46): full report = Contents, List of Figures and List of Tables; letter memo (up to
   10 pages, single topic) = figures inline after first citation, no lists; multi-section technical memo = contents,
   figures grouped at section end (default, to confirm).
3. JCO markup response: read every annotation page by page, log a response row for each comment
   (agency-comment-response for the log format and status vocabulary, D45), and save a copy of the marked-up PDF to
   the Standard's 40_QC T3 review folder as `<Job>_<ReportID>_<Milestone>_<YYYYMMDD>_JCO-Markup.pdf`.
4. Templates: reports use Report_Template 7.dotx (cover, TOC, heading and table styles, font); memos use
   _Electronic-Memo.doc (header, logo bar, formatting). Build to the template from the first draft, not a generic
   layout patched later.
5. Flag any missing input; never fill it silently; label all assumptions.

### 2. Report content rules
- **Plan deficiencies:** where the design differs from, or is deficient against, the current plan set, list each
  item and ask JCO how to handle it (revise plans, note in report, alternative). Never assume plan revisions.
- **Onsite watersheds** end at the property line; do not show offsite areas that drain away from the site. Existing
  and proposed total areas match to two decimals.
- **Nested areas:** list each catchment with its parent; state which outlet areas include upstream basins or pipe
  catchments; never sum flows across nested areas (one total-area scenario; with detention, route upstream outflow
  and add only the incremental downstream area).
- Areas not regraded (e.g. an existing yard) are modeled on **existing contours**.
- **Sources:** cite only real sources; references numbered 1), 2), ... with online links where available. Never
  mention superseded drafts, the calc workbook or Excel in the report.
- **Tc** is the hydrology-program value (PC-Hydro 5-min minimum). Never describe time to peak as Tc. Table values
  match native program output.
- **Rainfall tables** state source, statistic, return period and duration. Runoff-coefficient columns headed with
  the symbol (e.g. Cw) and plain numbers.
- **Channels (D27):** n = 0.025 applies to constructed unlined earthen channels; natural channels take n from land
  cover with the source cited. Show required depth (normal depth + required freeboard) vs provided; state lining
  (earthen/unlined) where applicable.
- **First flush** is provided below the outlet invert (raise the outlet inlet rather than regrade the basin); a
  shallow first-flush area up to 9 in deep may be added if needed.
- **Basin drawdown** = retained depth / tested infiltration rate with the standard factor of safety. Untested rate
  (D23): state the basis and the testing requirement; the jurisdiction method comes from the drainage-report-build
  add-on (Pima: required-rate method; Placer: half NRCS rate with 0 in/hr sensitivity).
- **Critical facilities (D22):** 0.2% (500-yr) WSEL from the FIS profile only if its cross sections bracket the
  site; else agency 500-yr hydrology; else a documented provisional value with agency agreement. Annotate the
  profile with project extents and the values used.
- **Maintenance/inspection plan:** include a preliminary plan only when the jurisdiction requires it; otherwise ask
  JCO.
- **Culvert/structure sizes** come from survey or as-builts; state the verified size, no discrepancy narrative.
- **Rise thresholds (D29)** are cited from the governing agency or stakeholder per project; no hard-coded value.
- **Independent checks (D30)** (spreadsheet or Python) live in 40_QC only, never in a deliverable.
- When two applicable standards conflict, flag it and apply the more restrictive value unless the code says
  otherwise.
- **Defined terms:** pick one term for project limits; define how vicinity, study limits and project area differ,
  or stop using the extras. Use defined section-zone terms (Top of Channel, Overbank Terrace, low-flow channel)
  only for those zones; run a term-count search before issue.

### 3. Report formatting
- **Page breaks** only before main sections (1.0, 2.0 ...) and appendices; pull text up to fill empty space; no
  half-empty pages, large white areas or orphaned headings (scroll the PDF to check). Template paragraph styles for
  spacing; no manual returns.
- **Tables (D47):** native Word tables, never screenshots; thin line borders on all cells (no heavy borders);
  header row in the template's header style; no alternating shading; no highlight fills; cell text centered; full
  text width; table titles centered.
- One caption per table, above the table, numbered by section (Table 4-1, D52); delete any second title inside
  the table; same caption-to-table spacing throughout. Fit tables to one page where possible; if a table breaks,
  repeat the header row.
- Keep wide tables portrait by dropping constant columns (state them in a note) or transposing single-row tables.
- **Precision:** elevations 2 decimals, no thousands separator; discharges whole cfs; keep stated precision
  (n = 0.025, slopes to 4 decimals); same precision down a column.
- "The ... is presented in Table n." sentences go at the **end of the preceding paragraph**. Resolve every
  table, figure and section cross-reference to the displayed number (Word fields, updated before export).
- **Figure and table numbering by section (D52)**: Figure 4-1, Table 4-1.
- **No report date in footers.** Title blocks carry no DRAFT date either (a changing date forces replotting the set).
- Abbreviate directions with a period (S.) or write road names out; be consistent. Spell out agency names on first
  use; one style for dollar amounts, model names (FLO-2D), ROW, dimensions (10 ft).
- Fix TOC tab alignment, stray characters and a missing firm heading bar (pull a fresh template if unsure).
- Cover: project-specific site photo, preferably from the field visit.
- **No indication of AI anywhere**: report text, calc sheets, printouts, file and document properties, folder names
  (use `<Initials>_<YYYYMMDD>_<topic>`). Preparer shown as "Psomas (JCO)" or the preparer's initials.
- Brand: Psomas colors and fonts. Office documents use Arial (fallback font). Primary Pacific Blue #0C3350;
  secondary California Poppy #EA7B24; support grays #8D9DA6 / #E3E9EA. If the brand package is not on hand, use
  neutral styling and make no brand claim.
- Deliverable text in completed tense (D44); placeholder pages only for named future items, labelled; no blank
  areas in the body (D50).

### 4. Exhibits, workmaps and figures

#### 4.1 Tool and sheet
1. **Tool (D37):** QGIS or CAD layouts for report exhibits. Scripted (Python) sheets are allowed for review,
   screening and result-map series that pass the same checks, with the editable source kept; build them with
   scripted-exhibit-sheets. Confirm with JCO before building whether others must edit the figures; if yes, QGIS or
   CAD from the start (default, to confirm).
2. **Baseline standard:** PCRFCD DS-305 workmap/exhibit standards except sheet size.
3. **Sheet sizes (D36):** report exhibits 11x17 (scalable to 22x34); CAD coordination exhibits 30x42 allowed when
   detail is lost at smaller sizes; appendix exhibits and memo inline figures 8.5x11 with the Psomas border.
4. Use the standard Psomas exhibit border. One orientation for all exhibits in a set, title block at the bottom;
   rotate the north arrow, not the sheet layout.
5. **Engineering scale:** viewport at 1 in = 50, 100, 200, 500 ft, etc., with a matching scale bar; measure the bar
   on the plotted sheet against the stated scale.
6. Multi-sheet exhibits: match lines and a sheet key (1 of 2, 2 of 2).
7. **Text (D34):** 9 pt minimum for new text; 0.1 in absolute minimum for inherited CAD text (default, to confirm).
8. Full-size 11x17 figure pages grouped at the end of their main section (full report).
9. **Labels:** call all graphics Figure or Exhibit (not both), numbered in order with none missing, matching the TOC;
   every exhibit has a number cited in the report text.
10. No pixelated raster images; export at plot resolution.
11. One template, one depth ramp and one overlay opacity fixed before the first sheet is rendered; finish the figure
    list before the first export.

#### 4.2 Standing map checklist (every map sheet)
- North arrow.
- Graphic scale bar (measured against the stated scale).
- Horizontal datum and vertical datum callouts (e.g. NAD83(HARN) Arizona Central, intl ft, EPSG:2868; NAVD88).
- Legend that defines every symbol and every raster or vector class interval, with units.
- Title block: firm, project no., figure no., title, scale, drawn/checked, source file (CAD-derived exhibits).
- Basemap source and year credit line (GIS/aerial exhibits); imagery date can differ from lidar date, credit both.
- Third-party data (soils, FIRM, NFHL) carry dataset or panel, effective or pull date, and datum.
- Borrowed photos and graphics carry a source credit in the caption.
- Any CRS assumed from file names or world files is stated on the sheet.

#### 4.3 Legends
1. Each entry shows the real mapped symbol (color, line weight and style, arrow, fill, hatch) with a concise feature
   label; no text descriptions of symbology.
2. Every symbol on the sheet (flow arrows, hatches, lines) appears in the legend; only symbols present on the sheet
   appear. If a layer has no features in the frame, drop its entry or state "none mapped".
3. Scripted or filtered layers are tested for a non-empty result before rendering; stop or warn on an empty layer.
4. Entries named by condition: existing vs proposed clearly separated; no ambiguous pairs ("Proposed Road" vs
   "Road Lines").
5. HEC-HMS subbasins shown distinctly from PC-Hydro watersheds when both appear.
6. Repeat a legend fix on every exhibit in the set.

#### 4.4 Base content and labels (drainage maps, watershed maps, result and floodplain exhibits)
1. Full aerial coverage of the sheet (exception: location/vicinity map, 4.6). Aerial at full strength (D40).
2. Label major roads on every exhibit plus a few local or subdivision roads; in sparse areas label landmarks
   (school, major adjacent parcel, the facility the project serves).
3. Label existing culverts and bridges, at-grade crossings, wash names and well sites.
4. Show existing and proposed drainage infrastructure with sizes: culverts (cells, size, type), channels, berm
   segments and raised-berm limits. Draw berms as thick colored lines with basic dimensions.
5. Label every structure number on drainage maps (Q not required on pavement drainage maps).
6. Label curb and scupper outfalls with arrows and Q values.
7. Show storm drains as storm drain (sketched from as-builts and aerials), not as part of the wash network. For
   offsite areas near a storm drain, show the storm drain, manholes and inlets, include roadway and upstream
   subdivision areas tributary to it, state the inlet capture assumption and label upstream offsite infrastructure.
8. Thicker watershed lines, flow direction arrows, wipeouts behind labels; keep labels inside the sheet.
9. Screen back contours so roads and labels stand out; solid or tight-dash lines; explain any red lines or remove
   them.
10. Proposed linework only for proposed; existing roads labelled or given a different linetype; layers named by
    condition. Proposed road and culvert linework shown on result maps.
11. Shade the subject parcel darker but not solid; label parks and neighbors; name parcels neutrally (parcel or
    owner type), never with draft or working labels.
12. Protected areas, property boundary, parcels, easements and named washes on every map sheet; add large-scale
    insets or typical sections where the text cites a corridor width.
13. Mark pending values as pending and unmodeled concepts as such on the sheet.

#### 4.5 Drainage map and watershed exhibit symbology
- Watershed boundaries: thick, dark/bright pink.
- Flowlines: cyan dashed with direction arrows; call it a flowline where no stream exists; show the Tc flow path.
- Sheet-flow arrows: short, with squiggly leaders.
- CP symbols by type. **CP labels (D41):** node letters plus Q100 on the map; full attributes (area, Tc, Q2-Q100,
  etc.) in the report table; descriptive attributes live in the shapefile (default, to confirm).
- Location-map labels aligned along the feature (river, road).
- Basin labels: required/provided first flush, 100-yr volume, depth and WSEL. Storage labels read "Volume Required"
  and "Calculated to Provide" from the register table (scripted-exhibit-sheets, register section).
- **Contours (D42):** watershed exhibits 1-ft minimum, 0.5-ft on flat sites; 2-ft only for large offsite areas.
  Other drainage maps: interval chosen by scale (1-ft small onsite). Result maps: 2-5 ft, screened.
- Topo on every watershed exhibit; boundaries follow visible ridge lines; highlight depressions and the flow line
  into them; flow arrows agree with contours.
- Onsite watershed boundary at the project boundary so pre vs post is shown there.

#### 4.6 Location, vicinity and project-area maps
1. **No aerial and no FEMA layers on the location/vicinity map (D35)** (explicit exception to full aerial coverage).
2. About 1 in = 3 mi, taken from the design plans when available, with township-section-range; major roads and
   landmarks labelled; crop location images to remove stationing and plan clutter.
3. One project-area map early in the report showing study limits, affected properties and reference features
   (canal, railroad, river, interstate), especially for long corridors with several study areas.
4. Explain regional study-area figures borrowed from master plans, or remove them.

#### 4.7 Result maps (2D depth, velocity, WSE, difference)
1. **Depth ramps (D31, D32)**, continuous bounds, upper bound exclusive (0.2 <= d < 0.5):

   | Ramp | Classes (ft) | Colors |
   |---|---|---|
   | local (default) | < 0.2 hidden; 0.2-0.5; 0.5-1.0; 1.0-2.0; 2.0-3.0; >= 3.0 | -, yellow, cyan, blue, orange, red |
   | deep-flow (regional washes, corridors) | 0-3; 3-5; 5-10; >= 10 | yellow, blue, orange, red (colors default, to confirm) |

   The exhibit states which ramp is used (legend title, e.g. "Max Depth (ft), local classes"). Ramp choice is
   default, to confirm.
2. **Masks (D33):** rasters keep the 0.01 ft data mask; the display cutoff is the bottom of the chosen ramp.
3. **Difference maps (D33):** proposed minus existing (or mitigated minus base). Show increases only; blank zero and
   decreases. Hide |d| < 0.10 ft unless the agency threshold differs (then show the 0-0.10 class in yellow). Classes:
   0.10-0.25 cyan, 0.25-0.50 green, 0.50-1.0 blue, 1.0-2.0 orange, >= 2.0 red (continuous bounds). Hatch newly wet
   ground separately or drop it on request. State on the sheet: sign, wet/dry rule (WSE difference only where both
   scenarios are wet; depth difference counts dry as 0 ft) and display threshold.
4. Pair a velocity change exhibit with every WSEL change exhibit.
5. **Opacity (D40):** aerial at full strength, result raster at 60% opacity (default, to confirm).
6. Legend range set to the classes above, never the raster min-max stretch; no 3-decimal breaks.
7. Check the max value before publishing; an implausible value (e.g. 48 ft on a piedmont) is a terrain or rendering
   artifact.
8. Same scale, classes and legend on existing and proposed sheets.
9. One exhibit set per storm analyzed in the text, with the storm in the title block.
10. Every model inflow location drawn as a cross-section line labelled with ID and peak Q for that storm; exhibit
    IDs cross-referenced to the design discharge table.
11. Base: aerial, contours (4.5), structure labels, easement notes, proposed road and culvert linework.
12. RAS Mapper screenshots carry the same labels as any other exhibit.
13. Fix class breaks with JCO before rendering, then push the same breaks into report text and tables in one change.
14. Label the water source on renderings and 3D views (1D/2D, plan, date) and the concept status.

#### 4.8 FEMA floodplain and FIRM content
1. Show FEMA SFHA extents (Zone AE and the 0.2% chance area) and BFE lines on project exhibits where present.
2. State the effective date of the mapping on the exhibit and in the text.
3. Pull effective FEMA layers for each exhibit extent; credit source and pull date. NFHL filter and layer details:
   `addons/fema.md`.
4. Empty subset: drop the legend entry or state "none mapped"; never issue a figure built on an empty filter.
5. Pending map revision: preliminary or work map as a separate labelled appendix item with its status; never shown
   as effective.
6. **FIRM panel / FIRMette marking (D39):** tight box or sketched alignment, labelled "this project", covering the
   whole project; a full panel only with the project marked tightly.

#### 4.9 CAD coordination and cut/boring exhibits (owner-team exhibits)
1. Clip master plan xrefs; show the actual site plan and survey; master plan linework in a distinct muted color so
   it does not read as survey.
2. Freeze unneeded layers (e.g. canopies); thicken key proposed lines; legend for existing vs proposed.
3. Label FF, FG and major contours; trace grading breaklines from the grading model.
4. 30x42 when detail is lost at a smaller sheet (D36).
5. When the architectural base changes, adjust the storm drain and say so on the exhibit.
6. Cut/boring exhibits: proposed cut at each test pit or boring; a note stating what the cut is measured to (bottom
   of foundation inside buildings, finished surface outside); max and min cut; color ramp with clearly different
   shades at key depths (e.g. 6 ft vs 8 ft).
7. Match table text size and properties across all tables on the sheet.

#### 4.10 Typical figure series
Location/Vicinity, Project Area, Aerial, Watershed/Offsite Basin, Hydrologic Soils, Existing- and Proposed-Conditions
Drainage Maps, Floodplain/FIRM, Result Maps (per storm), Difference Maps (with velocity change), Channel/Culvert
Profiles. Road profile exhibits: tangent grades between PVIs with percent grade labelled, not the raw grade-following
profile.

#### 4.11 Values on exhibits
Every Q, volume and invert label on an exhibit traces to one register row and matches the report table; regenerate
the exhibit from the register when values change (scripted-exhibit-sheets). Required vs provided shown for each
storage unit.

### 5. Native model output
- Run PC-Hydro (.pk6) natively in the PC-Hydro web app and include the native printouts and hydrographs, not recreated
  tables; user name "Psomas (<initials>)" (pchydro-hydrographs).
- HEC-HMS, HY-8, HEC-RAS, FLO-2D: include native program output; table values match it. EPA SWMM is an independent
  check only in AZ; SWMM/SSA primary only under the Placer add-on (D26).
- **Native output always in the appendix (D38).** A compact or extracted sheet may be added, labelled "extracted
  summary", with every value traced to the native file and the native file kept in the record.
- Final report: Word export with fields and TOC updated, then a bookmarked compiled PDF (body + appendix dividers +
  source printouts); verify every bookmark resolves (drainage-report-build).

### 6. Deliverables and QC
- Deliverables: report DOCX/PDF, compiled bookmarked PDF, stand-alone agency checklist (section numbers as displayed),
  appendix dividers, comment-response log (editable separate file plus bound copy where the agency asks, D49),
  updated calc workbook.
- Compiled PDF (D48, D52): author highlights flattened; inherited plan revision clouds removed (originals kept);
  third-party annotations flattened or noted; <= 50 MB per file or the agency limit if lower, split otherwise;
  bookmarks = cover, TOC, each main section, each appendix, each exhibit (default, to confirm).
- JCO reviews by redlining a compiled PDF placed in the job's 40_QC folder (not Word comments).
- Open items live in one internal QC open-items document (D44); compile is blocked while items are open unless JCO
  authorizes it.
- Before calling a report submittable: jurisdiction confirmed; plans match (or JCO decision recorded); independent
  calc check done; open items closed or authorized; waivers and approvals listed; seal block ready. Review sets show
  preliminary status only in the seal block per firm practice; body text stays in completed tense.
- Issued exhibits go to 10_Record\X_Exhibits with an ExhibitRegister row (figure ID); superseded sets to
  10_Record\_Superseded; increment the file suffix (v2, v3), never overwrite.

## Jurisdiction add-ons
Load with `get_skill("drainage-report-exhibit-standards", resource="addons/<file>.md")`:
- `addons/pima-county-rfcd.md`: Pima County RFCD exhibits (DS-305 notes, roadway outfall Q and berm labels,
  difference-map origin, CRS default). Load for any Pima County RFCD submittal.
- `addons/city-of-tucson.md`: design-plan Q and calculated Q at culverts; storm drain base and inlet capture on
  watershed exhibits. Load for City of Tucson work.
- `addons/town-of-marana.md`: project-area map and defined terms on corridor DCRs; CRS note. Load for Marana work.
- `addons/fema.md`: NFHL layers and field values, effective vs preliminary handling, FIRMette marking, work-map
  zones. Load whenever an SFHA, FIRM panel or CLOMR/LOMR work map is involved.
- `addons/placer-county-ca.md`: gallery register checks and coordination exhibits (Lake Tahoe Basin). Load for
  Placer County work.
Report-level jurisdiction rules stay in drainage-report-build add-ons.

## Gotchas
- Draft scale bar measured 2.4 in per 1,000 ft, not a usable scale; Rev A set 1 in = 200 ft on 11x17. (SAHPARK-008)
- A 30% DCR still had 17 Figure and 15 Exhibit labels side by side; about 25 reviewer comments were on legibility or
  legends. (BARNETT-008)
- Legends describing symbology in words were rejected and replaced with graphic samples. (NORTHLOOP-012)
- Legend shown with the full map checklist: north arrow, scale, datums, credits. (CAMPBELL-016)
- GeoPandas warned the 0.2% subset was empty and the figure was issued anyway. (CALFIRE-017)
- A BC-line filter returned an empty layer and BC lines silently dropped off an exhibit. (RKN-012)
- Draft legend: "Proposed Road" covered only the roundabout and "Road Lines" mixed existing and proposed. (SAHPARK-007)
- RAS screenshots were allowed early but still needed the full labels. (CAMPBELL-018)
- Draft exhibit had no road labels, no culverts and an ambiguous road legend; the destination facility the road
  serves was not labelled. (SAHPARK-007)
- Structure numbers were missing on all proposed drainage maps. (VALENCIA-023)
- 12 exhibit comments on three figures, several repeated on each figure; fix one figure and copy the fix to the rest.
  (TANGERINE-022)
- "Overbank" appeared 29 times in mixed meanings and "corridor" 44 times after the reviewer asked for defined
  limits. (BARNETT-007)
- Difference classes were re-cut three times (fine bands 0.1/0.15/0.2/0.25), and each change had to be pushed into
  the report too. (CAMPBELL-016)
- Default stretched legend showed breaks at 3 decimals and a 48.898 ft top bin from an artifact. (SAHPARK-006)
- Opaque raster hid the aerial base. (SAHPARK-006)
- Text said 10-yr and 100-yr were analyzed but only one unlabelled map was provided. (SAHPARK-009)
- 10-yr corridor depth mapping was not in the regional study record obtained; request it early. (SAHPARK-009)
- Draft exhibits omitted the FEMA floodplain entirely and the FIRM appendix held only the current panel. (SAHPARK-010)
- The project location box covered most of the FIRM panel. (SAHPARK-010)
- Repeated markups for line weight, legend and xref clutter across 8+ coordination exhibits. (HOMEWOOD-020)
- Three review rounds on a bore hole exhibit for missing cut labels and an unclear color ramp. (HOMEWOOD-019)
- The first existing drainage map lacked the standard symbology and had to be rebuilt by patch. (RKN-013)
- Flow arrows contradicted contours and one watershed boundary had no supporting ridge. (TANGERINE-023)
- Offsite watershed omitted roadway and subdivision areas tributary to the storm drain. (TANGERINE-024)
- Candidate areas 40.0, 27.8, 27.0 and 12.9 ac were nested; summing would roughly triple the flow. (EKOS-LOCAL-008)
- Local draft narrative started summing basin and road flows until guarded. (EKOS-LOCAL-008)
- Reports first built in a generic layout were restructured with one-time patches, about 1.25 h rework. (RKN-014)
- Table with green highlights, mixed elevation decimals and a table name not matching the caption. (SAHPARK-004)
- A screenshot of an Excel table plotted poorly. (SAHPARK-004)
- A short appendix table ran onto a second page. (SAHPARK-004)
- Excessive and inconsistent spacing between sections; a large blank area on one page. (SAHPARK-005, TANGERINE-018)
- Table mismatch flagged twice, extra space three times, a stray bracket and footer dates in one draft. (TANGERINE-018)
- A DRAFT date in every title block forced replotting the whole set when the date changed. (TANGERINE-006)
- First comparison exhibit was one 24x18 sheet with text legends; rebuilt to three 11x17 sheets (about 2 h).
  (NORTHLOOP-011)
- Brand package was not available; neutral styling used and no brand claim made. (NORTHLOOP-011)
- Image date can differ from lidar date; credit imagery source on each exhibit. (SILVERBELL-017)
- About 45 depth exhibit files were produced (v2-v6, three opacity variants, four sheets in two sizes and two
  orientations) because template, ramp and opacity were not fixed first. (ELTORO-015)
- Two class conventions (discrete 0.21-0.50 vs continuous 0.10-0.25) left cells in no class; continuous bounds with
  the upper bound exclusive close the gap. (SAHPARK-006, CAMPBELL-016; D32)
- A scripted figure set could not be edited by the user, who asked for QGIS or CAD recreation. (TANGERINE-006; D37)

## QC checks
- Pull rules: `get_qc_rules('exhibits')`, `get_qc_rules('report-text')`, `get_qc_rules('tables')`,
  `get_qc_rules('crs')`, `get_qc_rules('fema')` (SFHA present), `get_qc_rules('package')` (compile), plus the
  jurisdiction tag (`pima-rfcd`, `tucson`, `marana`, `sahuarita`, `placer`, `caltrans`).
- Exhibit checks this skill must pass (exhibit-reviewer runs them on a PNG render of every sheet, one complete pass
  logged per revision):
  - Standing map checklist (4.2) on every map sheet.
  - Scale bar measured on the plotted sheet = stated scale; engineering scale.
  - One label type (Figure or Exhibit), numbered by section, continuous, matches TOC and text citations.
  - One orientation and title-block position across the set; match lines and sheet key on multi-sheet exhibits.
  - Text >= 9 pt new, >= 0.1 in inherited CAD text; no pixelated images.
  - Legend: graphic sample for every symbol shown; no entry for absent symbols; no empty-layer warnings unresolved.
  - Major roads and landmarks labelled; every culvert labelled with cells, size, type; every structure numbered.
  - Existing vs proposed distinguishable by layer, linetype and legend; contours screened; no unexplained red lines.
  - Drainage maps: pink watersheds, cyan dashed flowlines with arrows, node letters plus Q100, HMS vs PC-Hydro basins
    distinct.
  - Watershed exhibits: contour interval per D42; every boundary segment supported by contours; arrows agree with
    contours; parent-child area table with incremental areas summing to the total.
  - Location map: no aerial, no FEMA layers, T-S-R, road labels; one project-area map near the front.
  - Result maps: ramp named and per D31; continuous bounds; display cutoff = ramp bottom; 60% raster over full-strength
    aerial; max value checked; one set per storm; inflow XS labelled with Q matching the discharge table.
  - Difference maps: increases only, |d| < 0.10 ft hidden (or agency value), sign and wet/dry rule stated, velocity
    change exhibit paired.
  - FEMA: SFHA and BFEs shown when present; effective date on sheet and in text; no empty NFHL subset; pending
    revisions separate and labelled; FIRM box tight or alignment sketched.
  - CAD coordination: master plan muted and distinct from survey; xrefs clipped; cut exhibits complete.
  - Every Q and volume label traces to a register row and matches the report table.
- Report checks: no image tables; one table style per D47; one caption per table; column precision consistent; no
  footer dates; no blank half pages; no orphaned headings; term-count search run; no AI indication in text or
  properties.

## Skill: scripted-exhibit-sheets v1.0.0

# Scripted Exhibit Sheets

One script per exhibit set renders every sheet from figure IDs, a register table and shared helpers
(`scripts/exhibit_kit.py`), so a style or value change re-renders the whole set. Standards (sheet, map checklist,
legends, ramps, base content) come from drainage-report-exhibit-standards; this skill is the production method.
exhibit-reviewer runs the review pass before compile.

## When to use
- Review, screening and result-map series (depth, velocity, WSE, difference, inflow and flow-rate exhibits)
  produced from GIS layers and model rasters (D37).
- Report exhibits only after JCO has accepted scripted figures for the job (decision log entry) and the editable
  source is kept; otherwise build report exhibits in QGIS or CAD (D37, default, to confirm).
- Any exhibit whose labels change with design iterations (peak Q at CPs or inflow points, storage required vs
  provided, inverts): drive labels from the register (Steps, section B).
- Mapping FLO-2D output (TOPO.DAT, DEPTH.OUT, MAXWSELEV.OUT, MapCrafter rasters) to depth/WSE exhibits (section C);
  FEMA zone delineation for work maps in `addons/fema.md`.

## Inputs
- Figure list: IDs (Figure 4-1 numbering by section, D52), titles, extents, storms, conditions. Finished before the
  first export.
- Editability decision (scripted vs QGIS/CAD) recorded in the job decision log.
- Layers in one CRS (Pima County default EPSG:2868, D55) with every .prj / world file checked.
- Basemap: current aerial (NAIP or local aerial service) with source and date; hillshade where useful.
- Model rasters from hecras-result-rasters (D43 names, dictionary) or FLO-2D outputs (flo2d-model-runs).
- Register CSVs: inflow register (ID, x, y, Q per storm), CP table (letter, Q100), storage register (unit, volume
  required, volume provided, footprint, inverts).
- Psomas border dimensions and brand colors (drainage-report-exhibit-standards section 3).
- Environment: EKOS GIS uv environment by full path (D11), `%GIS_PY%` = `C:\EKOS\gis\.venv\Scripts\python.exe`
  (path per 08_Platform_Builds/ENVIRONMENTS.md).

## Steps

### A. Sheet set
1. **Decide the path.** Ask JCO whether others must edit the figures. If yes, stop and build in QGIS or CAD from the
   start. If scripted, log "scripted sheets per D37" in the decision log with the series name.
2. **Freeze the figure list** (IDs, titles, extents, storms, conditions) before any export.
3. **Fix one template first** and do not change it mid-set: `ek.sheet("11x17", "landscape")` (8.5x11 for appendix
   and memo inline figures, D36); title block at the bottom with no dates; legend, north arrow, graphic scale bar,
   datum note and credit line in the right margin; 9 pt minimum text (`ek.MIN_TEXT_PT`, D34).
4. **Fix symbology before rendering any sheet:** one depth ramp (`ek.RAMPS["local"]` default, `"deep-flow"` for
   regional washes and corridors, D31), difference ramp (`ek.RAMPS["difference"]` or `ek.difference_ramp(<agency
   threshold>)`, D33), result opacity `ek.RESULT_ALPHA` = 0.60 over a full-strength aerial (D40). Shared helpers for
   watersheds (pink), flowlines (cyan dashed, arrows), sheet-flow arrows, CP labels (letter + Q100, D41).
5. **One CRS.** Reproject every layer to the project CRS; record any CRS assumed from file names or world files on
   the sheet (`ek.datum_note(..., crs_note=...)`).
6. **Guard every filtered layer** with `ek.require_nonempty(layer, name)` (stops) or `strict=False` (warns; drop the
   legend entry or state "none mapped"). Never render past an empty-layer warning without resolving it.
7. **Draw layers, then set the scale:** `ek.set_extent_to_scale(ax, cx, cy, ek.engineering_scale(extent_ft,
   map_in))` after all layers are drawn; assert `ek.measured_scale(ax)` equals the stated scale. Use the same scale,
   classes and legend on existing and proposed sheets.
8. **Base content on every map sheet:** protected areas, property boundary, parcels, roads (labelled), easements,
   named washes, culverts and structures with numbers, proposed linework on result maps; insets or typical sections
   where the text cites a corridor width (drainage-report-exhibit-standards 4.4).
9. **Legend:** `ek.legend_patches(ax, entries)` with graphic samples only for symbols present on the sheet;
   `ek.ramp_legend_entries(ramp)` for result classes; legend title names the ramp and units.
10. **Dense maps:** split into 1 of 2 / 2 of 2 sheets with match lines and a sheet key.
11. **One script, figure IDs as arguments:** `python make_exhibits.py F4-1 F4-2 ...` regenerates the set; never
    hand-edit an output.
12. **Save:** `ek.save_sheet(fig, folder, stem, meta)` writes `<stem>_v<n>.pdf`, `.png` (margin visible in both) and
    the source/extent JSON; it never overwrites. Combined PDF with one bookmark per figure. For presentations keep
    editable slides with native tables.
13. **Register and file:** issued sheets to 10_Record\X_Exhibits with an ExhibitRegister row (template figure ID);
    superseded sets to 10_Record\_Superseded. Keep the script, register CSVs and JSON with the issued set (the
    editable source, D37) in the job, never inside a delivered model folder.
14. **Review pass:** render all sheets to PNG in `40_QC\<Initials>_<YYYYMMDD>_exhibit_review\rev`, r2, r3 (figure ID
    and title in each PNG name) and hand to exhibit-reviewer. Record every finding before fixing; fix once and apply
    to every sheet sharing it; re-render the full set once.

### B. Values from one register (Q labels, required vs provided)
1. Keep each changing value set in one CSV: inflow register (inflow ID, location, Q per storm), CP table (letter,
   Q100), storage register (unit, Volume Required, Calculated to Provide, footprint, inverts).
2. Load with `ek.load_register(path, key)` (duplicate keys stop the run).
3. Place labels by script with `ek.callouts(ax, pts, labels)` (leader lines, minimum spacing, staggered rows), not
   fixed offsets; stagger offsite-watershed labels.
4. Inflow exhibits: every model inflow drawn as a cross-section line labelled with ID and the peak Q for that storm;
   exhibit IDs cross-referenced to the design discharge table.
5. Storage exhibits: "Volume Required" and "Calculated to Provide" per unit from the register; re-check outlet invert
   vs WQV each time a unit size changes.
6. Before issue: `ek.compare_register(register, report_rows, key, fields)` against the report discharge and volume
   tables; any mismatch stops issue.
7. When values change, update the register and regenerate the exhibit; never edit labels by hand.

### C. FLO-2D result mapping
Model runs and acceptance: flo2d-model-runs and model-run-supervisor (D04, D09). Mapping here:
1. Read TOPO.DAT, DEPTH.OUT and MAXWSELEV.OUT with `ek.read_flo2d_xyz(path)`; `ek.assert_cells_match(topo, depth,
   wse)` must pass.
2. Grid values on the model cell size with `ek.grid_cells(x, y, v, cellsize, bounds)`, using the bounds of a correctly
   tagged reference raster when one exists.
3. Before using any supplied raster (e.g. MapCrafter MAXIMUM_DEPTH.tif), compare arrays and CRS tags of apparent
   duplicates: `ek.same_array_different_crs(a, b, crs_a, crs_b)` True means one tag is wrong; resolve before use.
4. Take WSE directly from MAXWSELEV.OUT; never derive it from depth plus a different terrain.
5. Masks: `wet, shown = ek.flo2d_wet_masks(depth, wse, display_cutoff)`; dry cells have WSE coded 0; the display cutoff
   is the bottom of the chosen ramp (D33); keep cell edges visible (nearest-neighbor rendering at the model cell size).
6. Residual check: `ek.wse_residuals(topo, depth, wse, wet)` on wet cells only; investigate residuals beyond
   rounding.
7. FEMA context layers: clip S_FLD_HAZ_AR, S_BFE, S_XS, S_LOMR to the extent (drainage-report-exhibit-standards
   `addons/fema.md`). Context sheets stay internal until return period, condition and vertical datum are confirmed.
8. Zone AE/AO delineation and BFE contours for CLOMR/LOMR work maps: `addons/fema.md`.

## Jurisdiction add-ons
- `addons/fema.md` (this skill): depth-to-zone delineation, AE assignment, BFE contours and zone shapefiles from
  FLO-2D results for CLOMR/LOMR work maps. Load with
  `get_skill("scripted-exhibit-sheets", resource="addons/fema.md")`.
- Exhibit content add-ons (Pima RFCD, Tucson, Marana, FEMA, Placer) live in drainage-report-exhibit-standards.
- Town of Marana: project CRS NAD83 Arizona Central (intl ft) was used on a concept report; confirm per project.
  (TANGERINE-006)
- Placer County / Lake Tahoe Basin: storage register with outlet invert vs WQV recheck (section B5). (HOMEWOOD-018)

## Gotchas
- Scripted matplotlib PDFs could not be edited by the user, who later asked for the figures to be recreated in QGIS
  or CAD. (TANGERINE-006)
- Using Python instead of QGIS layouts is a deviation that must be logged for JCO decision. (RKN-012; D37)
- Three exhibit versions were exported within about 2.3 hr on submittal morning (v1, v2 adding Figure 12, v3 16 min
  later); finish the figure list before export. (TANGERINE-006)
- A DRAFT date in every title block forces replotting the whole set when the date changes. (TANGERINE-006)
- Reviewers found report-scale figures too dense and the Preserve boundary missing; full-size sheets and the Preserve
  polygon on every map closed three comments. (TANGERINE-006)
- Reviewer markup: move legend, scale bar and north arrow into the margin; show the margin in the PNG as well as the
  PDF; cut the top margin by 50%. (ELTORO-015)
- About 45 depth exhibit files were produced (v2-v6, three opacity variants, four sheets in 11x17 and 8.5x11,
  landscape and portrait) because template, ramp and opacity were not fixed first. (ELTORO-015)
- Fixed-offset labels overlapped; replaced with a callouts helper and staggered offsite-watershed labels. (RKN-012)
- A filter on BC line type returned an empty layer and BC lines silently dropped off an exhibit. (RKN-012)
- GeoPandas warned the 0.2% subset was empty and the figure was issued anyway. (CALFIRE-017)
- Road profile exhibit first showed the raw grade-following profile; reduce to tangent grades between PVIs and label
  percent grade. (RKN-012)
- Exhibit scripts were rerun about 6 times in one day; largest rework item after report formatting. (RKN-012)
- Image date can differ from lidar date; credit imagery source on each exhibit. (SILVERBELL-017)
- Eight review rounds were rendered in one day, r2 to r4 within 7 min; check all sheets in one pass before
  re-rendering. (SAH-019)
- File names were truncated in a review round; keep figure ID and title in the PNG name. (SAH-019)
- Four versions of the existing flow-rates exhibit carried 50-70 hand-placed labels each, re-placed for each extent
  and plan change. (ELTORO-016)
- Stormwater exhibit and gallery sizing reissued about 7 times with sizes drifting from the vendor calculators.
  (HOMEWOOD-018)
- Basin values on a comparison exhibit were still pending at issue; mark pending values as pending. (NORTHLOOP-011)
- A MapCrafter MAXIMUM_DEPTH.tif carried a California CRS tag (EPSG 3498) while its identical twin carried AZ Central
  EPSG 2223; compare arrays and CRS before use. (TANGERINE-008)
- WSE minus terrain minus depth showed large residuals driven by dry zero cells; compute residuals on wet cells only.
  (TANGERINE-008)
- Aerial EPSG came only from file names and world files; record that assumption on the sheet. (TANGERINE-008)
- Matplotlib resets axis limits when a layer is drawn; set the engineering-scale extent after all layers and check
  the measured scale, or the sheet scale and scale bar disagree. (SAHPARK-008, kit build test)

## QC checks
- Pull rules: `get_qc_rules('exhibits')`, `get_qc_rules('crs')`; `get_qc_rules('flo2d')` for FLO-2D maps;
  `get_qc_rules('fema')` for work maps and SFHA content; `get_qc_rules('hydraulics-2d')` for RAS result maps.
- This skill passes only when:
  - Editable-or-scripted decision recorded before build (D37).
  - All layers share one CRS; assumptions noted on the sheet.
  - Script log shows no unresolved empty-layer warning.
  - Measured scale = stated engineering scale on every sheet; scale bar drawn at that scale.
  - Existing and proposed sheets share scale, classes and legend; ramp named in the legend title.
  - Margin, legend, north arrow, scale bar, datum note and credit line visible in PDF and PNG.
  - Every Q and volume label traces to a register row; `compare_register` against the report tables returns no
    mismatch.
  - File suffix incremented; superseded set kept in 10_Record; ExhibitRegister updated; source/extent JSON saved.
  - FLO-2D: cell coordinates match across inputs; WSE from MAXWSELEV; wet-cell residuals checked; supplied raster CRS
    verified.
  - The full drainage-report-exhibit-standards checklist passes in the exhibit-reviewer pass.
- Self-test of the kit: `python scripts\exhibit_kit.py --selftest <scratch folder>` (ramps, bounds, empty-layer guard,
  FLO-2D readers, residuals, a sample 11x17 sheet).

## Skill: hecras-result-rasters v2.0.0

# HEC-RAS Result Rasters

Generates GeoTIFFs from a HEC-RAS 2D plan results HDF: **Depth (ft)**, **Velocity (fps)**, **WSE (ft)**,
optionally the terrain used for depth, plus difference rasters between two scenarios. The bundled engine is
`scripts/hecras_result_rasters.py` (v2.0.0). Exhibit symbology for these rasters is set by
drainage-report-exhibit-standards (Result maps); sheets are built per scripted-exhibit-sheets or in QGIS.

## When to use
- After a 2D plan has finished and passed the run acceptance gate (model-run-supervisor), to make max depth,
  velocity and WSE rasters for exhibits, sampling or delivery.
- To build proposed-minus-existing (or mitigated-minus-base) WSE, depth or velocity difference rasters.
- To check a received set of result rasters before mapping or sampling from it (step 9).
- Not for the regulatory 1:1 product: RAS Mapper stored maps remain the authoritative source; this engine is a
  fast reproducible export that must pass the RAS Mapper spot check (step 7).

## Inputs
- Plan results HDF (`<project>.p##.hdf`). **Always ask which plan.** Never assume it.
- Scenario token and event token for D43 names (e.g. `EX`, `PR`, `PR-Mitigated`; `10yr`, `100yr`). Tokens use
  letters, digits and hyphens only; the underscore separates tokens. Use the same token in the file name, the
  plan title and the dictionary.
- Grid size: 10 ft default; 3 ft (3.28 ft when preserving native 1 m) for hydraulics/grading detail per D54.
- Clip polygon (shapefile/GeoPackage) if the user names one; otherwise the full mesh extent.
- Output CRS: the model's native projection (read from the HDF). Reproject only on request (`--epsg`) and flag a
  zone mismatch. Pima County default is EPSG:2868 (D55); record the realization in the data log.
- Optional: RAS Mapper export of the modified terrain (`--terrain`) when the plan uses terrain modifications.
- Environment: the EKOS GIS uv environment, called by full path (D11), e.g.
  `%GIS_PY%` = `C:\EKOS\gis\.venv\Scripts\python.exe` (08_Platform_Builds/ENVIRONMENTS.md).

## Steps
1. **Discover plans.** In the project folder list `*.p[0-9][0-9].hdf`. If none, ask for the HDF path. Read each
   plan title if cheap (`Plan Data/Plan Information` attribute `Plan Title`); skip on error.
2. **Prompt.** Ask the user to pick one plan (one option per discovered HDF). Confirm scenario token, event token,
   grid size and clip polygon if not already given. Write the plan-number to token mapping into the job's data
   log before exporting.
3. **Run acceptance first.** The engine reads the plan HDF volume error before it builds any raster:
   - Final runs: limit 0.1 % (D09). Screening runs: `--screening` sets 0.5 %; screening rasters are never
     reported as final.
   - Above the limit the export is **refused** (exit code 2). `--vol-warn-only` writes a flagged diagnostic set
     (flag `VOL_ERROR_OVER_LIMIT` in the GeoTIFF tags and the dictionary); flagged rasters are not used in a
     deliverable.
   - A regional value above the limit is flagged even when the global number passes (opposing regional errors
     cancel in the global value).
   - If no volume accounting is found in the HDF (flag `VOL_NOT_FOUND`), read global and per-area Volume
     Accounting in HEC-RAS and record it before using the rasters. Also confirm the other QC-C21 items (outflow
     BC present, boundary vs structure flow split, event-to-event variation) through model-run-supervisor.
4. **Run the engine** (D43 names, default):
   ```
   "%GIS_PY%" scripts\hecras_result_rasters.py --hdf <PLAN>.p14.hdf ^
     --scenario EX --event 100yr --cellsize 10 --clip <CLIP>.shp --outdir <OUT> --terrain-out
   ```
   - Legacy plan-number names: `--naming plan --tag p14` gives `p14_MaxDepth_ft_10ft.tif` (v1 behavior).
   - `--area <NAME>` only if the HDF has more than one 2D area (the engine warns and uses the first otherwise).
   - `--epsg <code>` only for a non-native output CRS.
   - `--terrain <file>` to use a RAS Mapper terrain export (with modifications) instead of the basename match.
   - `--wet` sets the data mask (default 0.01 ft, D33). Do not raise it to the display cutoff; the exhibit sets
     the display cutoff (bottom of the chosen ramp).
   Outputs in `<OUT>`: `<scenario>_<event>_Depth_ft_<cell>ft.tif`, `..._Velocity_fps_...`, `..._WSE_ft_...`,
   `<scenario>_Terrain_ft_<cell>ft.tif` (with `--terrain-out`), `raster_dictionary.csv` (appended each run) and
   `spotcheck_<scenario>_<event>.csv`.
5. **Terrain check.** Read every WARN line. If the engine reports terrain modifications in the geometry or in the
   terrain HDF (flag `TERRAIN_MODS_NOT_APPLIED`), depth is wrong where the modifications are: export the modified
   terrain from RAS Mapper on the plan's geometry and rerun with `--terrain`. Confirm the basename-matched
   terrain is the one RAS Mapper shows for the geometry, every time (each scenario can use a different terrain).
6. **Print QC.** CRS, pixel size, NoData (-9999), valid count, min/max/mean per output (the engine logs these).
   Sanity-check magnitudes: an implausible max depth (e.g. 48 ft on a piedmont) is a terrain or rendering artifact
   and is found before any exhibit. Screen single-cell velocity spikes before quoting a peak velocity.
7. **RAS Mapper spot check (required, D57).** Open `spotcheck_<scenario>_<event>.csv` (10 wet points spread
   over the depth range), read depth, WSE and velocity at the same points from a RAS Mapper max map of the same
   plan and terrain, and fill the RAS Mapper columns. Note differences in the `note` column. Expect stepped
   depth at cell edges (flat per-cell WSE) and higher script velocity (face-velocity proxy). Keep the filled
   sheet in 40_QC. Rasters are not used in a deliverable until this sheet is filled.
8. **Difference rasters** (same grid, same clip and cell size for both sets):
   ```
   ...python.exe scripts\hecras_result_rasters.py --diff-base <OUT>\EX_100yr_WSE_ft_10ft.tif ^
     --diff-new <OUT>\PR_100yr_WSE_ft_10ft.tif --variable wse --outdir <OUT>
   ```
   Output: `<OUT>\Differences\PR-minus-EX_100yr_WSE_ft_10ft_Difference.tif`. Sign = new minus base, positive =
   increase (for mitigation sets: mitigated minus base, negative = improvement). WSE difference only where both
   scenarios are wet; depth and velocity differences count dry as 0 ft. Data are kept at full precision; the
   exhibit hides |d| < 0.10 ft unless the agency threshold differs (D33). Pair every WSE change raster with a
   velocity change raster.
9. **Received raster sets.** List entry dates inside every result zip and the model result-raster folder. Treat
   files or zips marked VOID, and copies older than the latest final zip, as superseded. Sort by entry dates, not
   file names. Build a table of variable x scenario x source zip x date; flag variables present only in a VOID set
   and date mismatches between variables in the final set. Map and sample only from the final set; list any
   variable that must be regenerated.
10. **Floodplain polygons** (when the project asks): polygonize depth >= 0.5 ft and drop parts < 0.25 ac
    (project criterion; confirm per project); proposed-minus-existing WSE with graded blocks masked.
11. **Deliver.** Copy GeoTIFFs and `raster_dictionary.csv` to the job folder (10_Record\E_... per the Standard
    folder tree). With a sampled point table, deliver a README and a field dictionary CSV (field, plan, scenario,
    variable, units, sign, source raster). Deliver the terrain raster per scenario so the receiver can recompute
    depth. State in the deliverable that velocity is a m
